content.text:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The centralization is the right instinct — `DisposableDomains` as a single home for the blocklist, reused by both the validator and the mapper, and `formatRiskFlag` reusing the existing `formatPossibleDuplicate`/`formatCapacityWarning` helpers is clean and idiomatic. One structural issue, though:

**Email-domain extraction is duplicated across the two call sites.** The logic that pulls the domain out of an email address —

```java
int at = email.lastIndexOf('@');
if (at < 0 || at == email.length() - 1) { ... }
email.substring(at + 1)
```

— now appears verbatim in both `EmailDomainValidator.isValid` (lines 21–25) and `OwnerMapper.isDisposableAdjacentEmail` (lines 74–78). This is the exact split-brain the new class was introduced to prevent: `DisposableDomains`' own javadoc says the knowledge is "kept in one place so the create-time validation and the owner risk flag agree on the same list," yet how each site derives the *domain* from an email is re-implemented independently. If that parsing ever needs to change (trimming, odd edge cases), the two can silently diverge.

Concrete fix: push the email-level entry points into `DisposableDomains` so the `@`-splitting lives once, next to the data it feeds:

```java
public static boolean isDisposableEmail(String email) { ... }
public static boolean isDisposableAdjacentEmail(String email) { ... }
```

Then `EmailDomainValidator` calls `isDisposableEmail(email)` and `OwnerMapper.formatRiskFlag` calls `DisposableDomains.isDisposableAdjacentEmail(owner.getEmail())` directly. That also removes `OwnerMapper`'s private `isDisposableAdjacentEmail(Owner)` helper, which is the one method in the file doing raw string-parsing rather than being a MapStruct `format*`/`@Named` mapping — domain-parsing logic sits more naturally in the util than embedded in the mapper interface.
